name: Adam
summary: The man formed from the ground and placed in Eden. He eats the forbidden fruit after Eve gives it to him; Genesis connects his disobedience with toil, mortality and expulsion from the garden. His family begins the genealogies that lead to Noah.

geography.origin: Ground outside the garden; location unspecified (Genesis 2:7–8)

name: Eve
summary: Adam’s wife, named as the mother of all living. She eats the forbidden fruit and gives it to Adam, bringing both into the judgment and expulsion narrative. After Cain kills Abel, she describes Seth’s birth as the gift of another child in Abel’s place.

name: Cain
summary: Adam and Eve’s son, a cultivator whose offering is not accepted as Abel’s is. He kills his brother and is sentenced to wandering, yet receives a protective mark against revenge. His later family and city begin a separate line of descendants.

name: Abel
summary: Adam and Eve’s son, a keeper of sheep whose offering God accepts. Cain kills him after the contrasting reception of their offerings, making Abel the victim of the first killing narrated in Genesis. Eve later names Seth in connection with the loss of Abel.

name: Seth
summary: Adam and Eve’s son born after Abel’s death; Eve describes him as another child appointed in Abel’s place. His family line, rather than Cain’s, is followed through Enoch and Methuselah toward Noah in Genesis 5.

name: Enoch
summary: Jared’s son and Methuselah’s father in Seth’s family line, distinct from Cain’s son Enoch. Genesis describes him as walking with God and says God took him, interrupting the genealogy’s repeated pattern of reporting each man’s death.

name: Noah
summary: Described as righteous and walking with God, Noah brings his family into the ark through the flood. God’s covenant afterward promises no further flood to destroy all flesh and gives the rainbow as its sign. His later drunkenness leads into the episode in which he curses Canaan.

residence: Mountains of Ararat after the flood

name: Shem
summary: Noah’s son who survives the flood with his wife. With Japheth he covers Noah without looking at his nakedness; Noah’s subsequent words bless the God of Shem. His genealogy leads through Terah to Abraham.

name: Ham
summary: Noah’s son and the father of Cush, Mizraim, Put and Canaan. He sees Noah’s nakedness and tells his brothers; after waking, Noah curses Canaan, Ham’s son. Genesis 9 names Canaan as the recipient of that curse, not Ham.

name: Japheth
summary: Noah’s son who survives the flood with his wife. He and Shem cover their father while avoiding looking at his nakedness. Noah’s ensuing words ask God to enlarge Japheth and connect his future with Shem’s tents.

name: Terah
summary: Father of Abram, Nahor and Haran, and grandfather of Lot. He leads Abram, Sarai and Lot out of Ur toward Canaan but settles and dies in Haran. His household provides the family setting for Abraham’s journey and later marriage connections.

name: Abraham
summary: Also called Abram; the recipient of promises of land, descendants and blessing for the families of the earth. The covenant narrative introduces circumcision and identifies Isaac as Sarah’s promised son. Abraham’s willingness to offer Isaac becomes a central test, stopped before the child is killed.

name: Sarah
summary: Also called Sarai; Abraham’s wife and the mother of Isaac, born in their old age as the promised covenant child. Abraham also identifies her as his paternal half-sister. Her conflict with Hagar and demand that Hagar and Ishmael leave shape the household’s inheritance story.

name: Lot
summary: Haran’s son and Abraham’s nephew, who escapes Sodom with his wife and two daughters. His unnamed wife looks back and becomes a pillar of salt. Later his daughters become pregnant by him; their sons Moab and Ben-ammi are presented as ancestors of the Moabites and Ammonites.

name: Hagar
summary: Sarah’s Egyptian servant, given to Abraham as a wife, and the mother of Ishmael. She flees Sarah’s harsh treatment and receives a promise of numerous descendants. Later expelled with Ishmael, she encounters divine provision in the wilderness as his future is reaffirmed.

name: Ishmael
summary: Abraham and Hagar’s son, promised numerous descendants and twelve princes, while the covenant is assigned to Isaac. Sent away with Hagar, he survives in the wilderness and becomes an archer. His descendants form a distinct branch of Abraham’s family.

name: Isaac
summary: Abraham and Sarah’s promised son and the father of Esau and Jacob with Rebekah. He survives Abraham’s attempted offering when a ram is substituted. Later, Jacob’s deception leads Isaac to give him the blessing intended for Esau, intensifying the brothers’ conflict.

geography.origin: Abraham’s household; location not explicitly named at birth

name: Rebekah
summary: Bethuel’s daughter and Laban’s sister, who agrees to leave her family and marry Isaac. An oracle about her twins says the elder will serve the younger. She later helps Jacob obtain Isaac’s blessing by disguising him as Esau.

name: Esau
summary: Isaac and Rebekah’s older twin, also called Edom. He sells his birthright to Jacob for a meal, then loses his father’s blessing through Jacob’s deception. Though he initially intends revenge, their later reunion is an embrace; Genesis traces his family’s settlement in Seir.

name: Jacob
summary: Isaac and Rebekah’s son, later named Israel, and the father of twelve sons and Dinah. His deception over Esau’s blessing drives him from home; encounters at Bethel and his wrestling encounter frame his return. He reconciles with Esau, while his children’s rivalries lead the family toward Egypt.

name: Leah
summary: Laban’s elder daughter, given to Jacob before Rachel in a marriage Jacob says was arranged deceptively. Her search for affection and rivalry with Rachel shape the household. She bears six sons, including Levi and Judah, and the daughter Dinah.

name: Rachel
summary: Laban’s younger daughter and Jacob’s loved wife, whose rivalry with Leah includes giving Bilhah to Jacob. After a period without children she bears Joseph. She dies giving birth to Benjamin and is buried on the way to Bethlehem.

name: Bilhah
summary: Rachel’s servant, given to Jacob as a wife, and mother of Dan and Naphtali. Her sons become two of the family lines associated with Israel’s tribes. Reuben later sleeps with her, an act recalled in Jacob’s condemnation of his firstborn.

name: Zilpah
summary: Leah’s servant, given to Jacob as a wife during Leah and Rachel’s rivalry over children. She bears Gad and Asher, whose births Leah celebrates through their names. Those sons become two of the family lines associated with Israel’s tribes.

name: Reuben
summary: Jacob and Leah’s firstborn, who intervenes to stop his brothers from killing Joseph. He also sleeps with Bilhah, his father’s concubine. Jacob’s final words explicitly connect that act with Reuben’s loss of preeminence.

name: Simeon
summary: Jacob and Leah’s son, who joins Levi in killing the men of Shechem after Dinah’s violation. Jacob later condemns their violent anger and announces their scattering. In the Joseph narrative, Simeon is held in Egypt while his brothers return for Benjamin.

name: Levi
summary: Jacob and Leah’s son, who joins Simeon in the attack on Shechem after Dinah’s violation. Jacob’s final words condemn their violent anger and speak of their scattering in Israel. He is the named ancestor of the Levi family line, one of Israel’s tribal ancestors.

name: Judah
summary: Jacob and Leah’s son who proposes selling Joseph rather than killing him. In Tamar’s story he acknowledges that she is more righteous than he is; later he offers himself in Benjamin’s place. Jacob’s final words associate Judah with leadership, a lion and the sceptre.

name: Dan
summary: Jacob and Bilhah’s son, named by Rachel in connection with God’s judgment in her favor. He becomes a tribal ancestor. Jacob’s final words say Dan will judge his people and use the image of a serpent striking a horse’s heels.

name: Naphtali
summary: Jacob and Bilhah’s son, named by Rachel in connection with her struggles with Leah. He becomes a tribal ancestor. Jacob’s final words portray Naphtali as a released doe and associate him with beautiful words.

name: Gad
summary: Jacob and Zilpah’s son, whose birth Leah celebrates with a name linked to a troop in the KJV. He becomes a tribal ancestor. Jacob’s final words describe Gad as attacked by a troop but overcoming at the last.

name: Asher
summary: Jacob and Zilpah’s son, named by Leah in connection with her happiness. He becomes a tribal ancestor. Jacob’s final words associate Asher with rich food and royal delicacies.

name: Issachar
summary: Jacob and Leah’s son, born during the household rivalry involving Leah, Rachel and the mandrakes. He becomes a tribal ancestor. Jacob’s final words compare him to a strong donkey and connect pleasant land with bearing burdens and tribute.

name: Zebulun
summary: Jacob and Leah’s sixth son, whose birth Leah links to her hope of being honored by her husband. He becomes a tribal ancestor. Jacob’s final words associate Zebulun with the seashore, ships and a border toward Sidon.

name: Joseph
summary: Jacob and Rachel’s son whose dreams deepen his brothers’ hostility before he is sold into Egypt. After imprisonment he rises to authority under Pharaoh and manages grain supplies for famine. His reunion with his brothers brings the family to Egypt, and he interprets his suffering as part of preserving their lives.

name: Benjamin
summary: Jacob and Rachel’s youngest son, born as Rachel dies; Jacob gives him the name Benjamin rather than Ben-oni. Joseph’s demand to see him and the planted cup test his brothers’ loyalties, leading Judah to offer himself in Benjamin’s place. He becomes a tribal ancestor.

name: Dinah
summary: Jacob and Leah’s daughter, whose violation by Shechem leads to marriage negotiations and a deadly response by her brothers Simeon and Levi. Their attack and Jacob’s reaction make her story central to the family’s conflict with Shechem.

name: Tamar
summary: Judah’s daughter-in-law, widowed after marriage to Er and then Onan, and denied the promised marriage to Shelah. She disguises herself and becomes pregnant by Judah, retaining his possessions as evidence. When accused, she reveals them; Judah acknowledges her claim, and she bears Perez and Zerah.

name: Paul
summary: Also called Saul, a persecutor of Jesus’ followers who becomes a witness to Jesus and a missionary to the Gentiles. Acts follows his missionary work and imprisonment through his arrival in Rome. His letters identify him as an apostle and address Gentile inclusion, faith and the law, the resurrection, and the life of the communities he writes to.

name: Satan
summary: An adversary who challenges Job’s faithfulness and is permitted to test him within limits; Zechariah depicts Satan opposing the high priest. In the New Testament he tempts Jesus and is identified with the Devil. Revelation identifies the dragon and ancient serpent with Satan and portrays his final defeat. These passages give different narrative settings; Genesis itself does not name its serpent Satan.

geography.origin: No birthplace or human parentage specified in these passages
residence: Appears in the heavenly assembly and describes roaming the earth (Job 1:6–7)

name: Elisha
summary: Shaphat’s son from Abel-meholah, called from plowing to follow Elijah and recognized as his successor after taking up his mantle. His stories include provision for a widow, restoring a child to life, Naaman’s healing, and a curse followed by bears mauling forty-two mockers. He also intervenes in royal affairs and sends a prophet to anoint Jehu.

residence: Follows Elijah after leaving his farm (1 Kings 19:19–21)

name: Moses
summary: A Levite born in Egypt, adopted by Pharaoh’s daughter, and called at the burning bush to lead Israel out of Egypt. He leads the people through the sea and mediates the Sinai covenant and law. After the wilderness journey, he is barred from leading Israel into Canaan because of the Meribah episode; he dies in Moab, and Joshua succeeds him.

geography.origin: Egypt; hidden by the river as an infant (Exodus 2:1–10)

name: Joshua
summary: Nun’s son from Ephraim, also called Oshea and Jehoshua, who serves Moses and is commissioned as his successor. He leads Israel across the Jordan and in the conquest narratives, including Jericho’s capture and the killing of its inhabitants. His leadership also concerns dividing the land and renewing the covenant at Shechem, where he calls the people to choose whom they will serve.

geography.origin: An Ephraimite; birthplace not specified in the cited passages (Numbers 13:8)
residence: With Moses during the wilderness journey (Numbers 11:28)

name: Elijah
summary: A Tishbite from Gilead who announces drought and confronts Ahab and the worship of Baal. At Carmel, fire consumes his offering and he orders the captured prophets of Baal killed. After fleeing into the wilderness, he encounters God at Horeb and calls Elisha; his story ends with his being taken up by a whirlwind as a fiery chariot separates them.

name: Aaron
summary: Moses’ older brother and spokesman, appointed with his sons to the priestly office. While Moses is on the mountain, Aaron makes the golden calf and proclaims a feast, making him central to that breach of worship. Like Moses he is barred from entering Canaan after Meribah; his priestly garments pass to Eleazar before he dies on Mount Hor.

geography.origin: Born to Amram and Jochebed in Israel’s Egyptian setting (Exodus 6:20)
residence: Egypt during the confrontation with Pharaoh (Exodus 7:7)

name: Miriam
summary: Moses and Aaron’s sister, identified as a prophetess who leads the women in song and dance after the sea crossing. She and Aaron later challenge Moses; the account describes her becoming leprous, Moses praying for her healing, and the camp waiting through her seven-day exclusion. She dies and is buried at Kadesh.

geography.origin: Daughter of Amram and Jochebed in the Exodus family (Numbers 26:59)
residence: With Israel after the sea crossing (Exodus 15:20–21)

name: Job
summary: A man from the land of Uz, described as upright and fearing God. He loses his children, possessions, and health, disputes his friends’ explanations of his suffering, and addresses God. After God answers him, Job prays for his friends and the closing account describes the restoration of his fortunes and family.

children: Seven sons and three daughters in the opening account
Seven sons in the closing account (unnamed)

geography.origin: Land of Uz (Job 1:1); precise location unspecified

name: Jesus
summary: Jesus is born in Bethlehem to Mary and grows up in Nazareth. John baptizes him in the Jordan, and he begins teaching in Galilee. He calls twelve disciples and teaches in parables and the Sermon on the Mount. The Gospels describe miracles, such as turning water into wine, calming a storm and raising Lazarus. They call him the Christ and the Son of God. John’s Gospel calls him the Word, who "was with God, and the Word was God." He is crucified under Pontius Pilate and buried. The Gospels report that he rose on the third day and appeared to his followers. He sends them to baptize "in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost."
